mutants.why: smartctl's SATA device type is the token "sat" (upper-cased to "SAT"); comparing against the already-normalized "SATA" never matches, so interface_type stays "SAT". parseOutput_validSataJson asserts QCOMPARE(report.interface_type, QStringLiteral("SATA"))

the model lives under the JSON key "model_name"; reading "model" yields an absent value so report.model becomes empty. parseOutput_validSataJson asserts QCOMPARE(report.model, QStringLiteral("Samsung SSD 860 EVO"))

passed==true must map to "PASSED"; inverting labels a passing drive "FAILED" (and a failing one "PASSED"). parseOutput_validSataJson asserts QCOMPARE(report.smart_status, QStringLiteral("PASSED")) and Healthy; assess_smartStatusFailed asserts Critical for passed:false

inside the power_on_time object the count is under "hours"; reading "power_on_hours" there is absent so the value defaults to 0. parseOutput_validSataJson asserts QCOMPARE(report.power_on_hours, static_cast<int64_t>(12'000))

the raw counter is the "value" member of the raw object; reading "worst" (absent there) makes every raw_value 0, collapsing the whole warning/critical ladder and the reallocated-sector metric to zero. healthAssessment_critical asserts overall_health Critical AND QCOMPARE(report.reallocated_sectors, 50) at raw 50; healthAssessment_warning asserts Warning at raw 10

attribute id 5 is Reallocated_Sector_Ct; changing the routed id to 4 means the id-5 entry never populates report.reallocated_sectors, which stays 0. healthAssessment_critical asserts QCOMPARE(report.reallocated_sectors, static_cast<int64_t>(50)) and warnings.contains("Reallocated sectors detected: 50")

an attribute is failing only when it has a real threshold AND its normalized value has fallen to/below it; with || any attribute that merely declares a positive threshold is flagged failing. parseOutput_validSataJson (thresh:10, value:100) asserts QVERIFY(!attr.failing) and overall_health Healthy -- with || failing becomes true and health flips to Critical

the critical verdict must fire AT the critical raw threshold; relaxing >= to > lets a raw value exactly equal to critical_raw escape to mere Warning. healthAssessment_critical asserts overall_health Critical at raw 50 == critical_raw 50 for id 5

the warning verdict must fire AT the warning raw threshold; relaxing >= to > lets a raw value exactly equal to warning_raw read as Healthy. healthAssessment_warning asserts overall_health Warning at raw 10 == warning_raw 10 for id 199 (and Healthy at raw 9)

media_errors is a fault count -- Critical only when it exceeds zero; >= 0 is always true so every NVMe drive reads Critical. parseOutput_validNvmeJson (media_errors:0) asserts QCOMPARE(report.overall_health, sak::SmartHealthStatus::Healthy)

the guard must bail out ONLY on a parse error; inverting it aborts every well-formed document early, returning an empty (default) report for valid input. parseOutput_validSataJson then sees an empty report and fails QCOMPARE(report.model, QStringLiteral("Samsung SSD 860 EVO"))

ANY one SMART signal (status, attribute, or NVMe log) makes a report assessable; requiring status AND attributes together (via && precedence over the trailing || nvme) makes a status-only report non-assessable and forces Unknown. reportHasAssessableData_signalDetection asserts QVERIFY(reportHasAssessableData(with_status)) for a status-only report; parseOutput_missingFields asserts that a status-only payload is Healthy
